metadata.note: The Peoria and Eastern Railway and its predecessor the Indianapolis, Bloomington and Western, drawn from research/branches/peoria_and_eastern_railway.txt (researched 2026-10-31) in the companion site repo and converted the same day. Before this layer the map drew no Peoria - Indianapolis or Indianapolis - Springfield OH line. The P&E only OWNED its line and never ran its own trains, so features are named and coloured for who did: the Indianapolis, Bloomington and Western (and its 1879 and 1887 reorganisations, one railroad) to 1 July 1890, the Big Four to 1 February 1930, the New York Central after. Rule 4 splits share identical geometry. Big Four and NYC colours are pulled programmatically from existing features; the IB&W colour is new.
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 (cached OCR research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt): Table 24 'Peoria, Bloomington and Indianapolis', dated 2 Dec 1951, trains 11/12
Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 (cached OCR): Table 17 'Indianapolis, Crete and Springfield' headed 'Freight Service only', and the Index of Stations freight-only daggers (Arcanum, Farmers)
metadata.geometry_method: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (mail.ru mirror, cached degree tiles) plus OpenHistoricalMap (CC0) and OSM rail-trail ways, traced with opstrace.py: ways tagged old_railway_operator=NYC (the tag OSM uses for the P&E and Big Four) costed 1x, untagged rail and abandoned grade 1.25x, OHM ways 2-12x by name, cycleways 3x, other named operators 12x; waypoints geocoded with Nominatim (every result's type checked; Clermont IN hand-pinned, two Peoria river-bridge points pinned), simplified with Douglas-Peucker at 8 m and reversal-trimmed.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: OPEN END: Big Four Indianapolis - Springfield OH stops at 1896, the last CONFIRMED passenger year (Fowler 'Hunter 1896t'); passengers certainly rode later (a 1934 NYC working timetable shows passenger-carrying freights terminating at Eastside, Indianapolis) and the line was freight only by the Feb 1952 Guide, but no source dates the end. A 1910s-20s Official Guide or the 1934 NYC working timetable would settle it. Peoria cutback: 1955 (Wikipedia, chicagorailfan, Fowler) vs a 1956 Indianapolis board showing the Corn Belt Special to 'Peoria'. Exact last day of the Corn Belt Special (c. 14 Oct 1957, photo caption only). 1869 opening month: July (Wikipedia) vs 1 October (american-rails, twainsgeography). Springfield line opening: 1881/1882/1883 conflict, drawn from 1883. Whether IB&W trains reached Peoria before Peoria Union Station opened in 1882. All headways except the 1942 and 1951 counts, and all speeds except the 1951 NYC timing, are estimates. Station-level data (Rule 8) has not been started for this railroad.
metadata.branches_deliberately_omitted: NYC Indianapolis - Springfield mixed-train era (1930-?): the 1934 working timetable proves passengers rode freights on the Indianapolis end but not how far - drawable NONE until a timetable shows the stations. IB&W leased lines Springfield - Columbus OH and Springfield - Sandusky OH: IB&W operation dates unknown, drawable NONE. Amtrak Indianapolis - Crawfordsville (Cardinal/Hoosier State on CSX) is an Amtrak feature, not a P&E one.
metadata.freight_only_excluded: Indianapolis - Springfield OH after the last confirmed passenger year (Feb 1952 Guide Table 17 'Freight Service only'); the main line after October 1957 (freight under NYC, Penn Central, Conrail, CSX/NS until abandonments 1973-2004); Peoria - Pekin after the 1955 cutback; the unverified 1959 'last passenger movement through Urbana'.

properties.geometry_quality: 202.1 mi drawn Pekin - Indianapolis Union Station against the ICC valuation's 201.548 mi (122.782 Pekin - state line + 78.766 state line - Indianapolis) and Fowler's mileposts (Pekin 9.0 - Indianapolis 211.4 from Peoria = 202.4). NO straight-line legs. Composition (before simplification, 202.9 mi): 121.5 mi on ways OSM tags old_railway_operator=NYC (live Danville Secondary / Urbana Subdivision / Mansfield Branch track, abandoned grade and NYC-tagged rail-trail); 33.8 mi Pekin - Bloomington on an OpenHistoricalMap way dated 1869-11-25 to 1984-08-01 (the P&E grade, lifted 1984; it has no name tag) plus 1.2 mi of other unnamed OHM ways; 35.2 mi on untagged OSM rail or abandoned grade, chiefly Le Roy - Farmer City - Mansfield (~17 mi, ~200 m from an OHM way named Indiana, Bloomington and Western) and Ogden - Oakwood (~9 mi, where the Kickapoo Rail Trail is not yet mapped); 5.6 mi on OHM ways labelled 'Chicago, Danville and Vincennes Railroad' at Urbana and Oakwood (they lie on the P&E's own east-west alignment, so the OHM name looks wrong) and 'Indianapolis, Bloomington and Western Railway' at Speedway; 4.3 mi of rail-trail ways without the NYC tag (Kickapoo Rail Trail, Circle Trail at Covington, Sugar Creek Trail at Crawfordsville, Pekin Park Bike Trail); 0.8 mi on Nickel Plate (ex-Lake Erie and Western) track through Bloomington; 0.5 mi of short connectors. segments.note: The Indianapolis, Bloomington and Western, formed 20 July 1869 from the Danville, Urbana, Bloomington and Pekin and the Indianapolis, Crawfordsville and Danville, ran its own trains Pekin - Bloomington - Le Roy - Farmer City - Mansfield - Mahomet - Urbana - Danville - Covington - Crawfordsville - Indianapolis (not via Saybrook). Opened in 1869: Wikipedia says July, american-rails and twainsgeography say 1 October - the month conflicts, the year does not; partial openings of individual stretches earlier were not checked. The same railroad was foreclosed and renamed twice - Indiana, Bloomington and Western in 1879 and Ohio, Indiana and Western in November 1887 - one continuous operating company, so not a Rule 4 split. Nicknamed 'I Better Walk'. Ends 1 July 1890, when the Big Four took over operation for the new Peoria and Eastern. Fowler confirms stations in the 1870, 1875 and 1884 Official Guides and the 1876 Rand McNally. Headway is an ESTIMATE, not from a timetable (Rule 3).
sources: Segment-level: 1869 opening from Wikipedia (July) vs american-rails and twainsgeography (1 Oct), conflict recorded; 1 Jul 1890 end from american-rails; in-era stations from Fowler (1870G, 1875G, 1876 Rand McNally, 1884G). Headway NOT SOURCED.

segments.note: The Indiana, Bloomington and Western's eastern extension (ex-Ohio, Indiana and Pacific / Indianapolis and Ohio State Line project), Indianapolis - Mount Comfort - Shirley - New Castle - Mooreland - Lynn - Crete - Arcanum - Ludlow Falls - Troy - New Carlisle - Springfield OH, run by the IB&W and from November 1887 by its reorganised successor the Ohio, Indiana and Western (same railroad, not a split). segments.note: Peoria and Eastern main line, Pekin - Bloomington - Champaign/Urbana - Danville - Crawfordsville - Indianapolis, owned by the Peoria and Eastern Railway (incorporated Feb 1890) but operated from 1 July 1890 by the Cleveland, Cincinnati, Chicago and St. Louis ('Big Four'); the P&E never ran its own trains. Ends 1 February 1930, when the New York Central leased the Big Four. NYC's stock control of the Big Four from 1905-06 did not change who ran the trains and is not a split. In-era evidence: Fowler's 'Chicago & Alton Crossing 1896t' (Big Four company timetable), 'Urbana Yard 1923G', 'Lyons 1915w'. Through trains ran on to Peoria over the P&PU (separate feature). Headway is an ESTIMATE, not from a timetable (Rule 3).
sources: Segment-level: 1 Jul 1890 start and 1 Feb 1930 end from american-rails; in-era service from Fowler (1896t, 1915w, 1923G). Headway NOT SOURCED.

END IS OPEN: 1896 is the last CONFIRMED year of passenger service (Fowler 'Hunter 1896t', a Big Four company timetable), NOT a known end - no source dates when passenger service actually stopped. The line demonstrably carried passengers later: Fowler's 'Eastside 1934w+' records passenger-carrying freight trains terminating at Eastside, Indianapolis, in a 1934 NYC working timetable, but how far they ran is unknown, so it is not drawn. By the Feb 1952 Official Guide (Table 17) the line was freight only. Do not extend without evidence. Penn Central abandoned the line in 1976 (freight, context only). Headway is an ESTIMATE, not from a timetable (Rule 3).

segments.note: One train each way, Nos. 11/12, the 'Peorian': the Feb 1952 Official Guide, Table 24 'Peoria, Bloomington and Indianapolis' dated 2 Dec 1951, shows times (Peoria Union Station lv 7:15, Mansfield, Mahomet, Veedersburg, Waynetown, Crawfordsville 11:29, New Ross). About 1955 the train was cut back from Peoria to Pekin and renamed the Corn Belt Special. Passenger service ended in 1957: railarchive.net dates the last westbound No. 11 'October 14, 1957 (or close to it)' and the train was photographed at Bloomington in June and October 1957; Wikipedia (Peoria Union Station), chicagorailfan and american-rails agree on 1957. american-rails' unsourced 'last passenger movement through Urbana' in 1959 is probably a special and is NOT drawn. Freight continued: Speedway - Clermont out c.1973, Crawfordsville - Olin 1982, Bloomington - Pekin 1984, Danville - Urbana 1996 (context only).
sources: Segment-level: Dec 1951 service and one train each way from the Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 24 (times visible); 1957 end from railarchive.net photo captions (Jun and Oct 1957), Wikipedia, chicagorailfan, american-rails.
